column2: Unit testing in CI/CD is the same three steps regardless of which flavor of evaluation you're running:
1. **Load your dataset** — pull goldens from Confident AI, a CSV, or a JSON file. This step is identical for every flavor.
3. **Run your test file** — same command for every flavor. Drops into a `.yml` file unchanged.
`deepeval` loads datasets from Confident AI, a CSV, a JSON file, or directly in code into an `EvaluationDataset`.
For [multi-turn](/docs/evaluation-end-to-end-multi-turn) evals, use `ConversationalGolden` instead of `Golden`. See [the datasets page](/docs/evaluation-datasets#load-dataset) for the full surface.

Pick the flavor that matches your application — [single-turn](/docs/evaluation-end-to-end-single-turn) (one input → one output) or [multi-turn](/docs/evaluation-end-to-end-multi-turn) (whole conversations).

Within single-turn, we strongly recommend **instrumenting your app with tracing** so `deepeval` can build the `LLMTestCase` automatically from each run, and you get a full per-test-case trace on Confident AI for free.

The same setup also unlocks [component-level evaluation](/docs/evaluation-component-level-llm-evals), where metrics live on individual spans (retrievers, tool calls, sub-agents) instead of the trace as a whole.

The golden goes to `expect()`, and `toPass()` takes:
- `options.run`: a callback `(golden) => ...` that runs your app so the matcher can capture and score its trace.
See [component-level evaluation](/docs/evaluation-component-level-llm-evals) for the per-integration metric attachment surface; trace-level and span-level metrics coexist in the same test run.
There are **TWO** mandatory and **ONE** optional parameter for `assert_test()` in this mode:
- `test_case`: an `LLMTestCase` you constructed inside the test.
- `metrics`: an array of `BaseMetric`s, run concurrently against the test case.

The fields you populate on `LLMTestCase` must match what your metrics need (e.g. `FaithfulnessMetric` requires `retrieval_context`). See [test cases](/docs/evaluation-test-cases#llm-test-cases) for the full parameter list.

Pick this if your app is multi-turn — chatbots, support agents, and any conversational app where the unit of evaluation is the whole conversation rather than a single exchange. You wrap your chatbot in a `model_callback`, simulate conversations against goldens, then evaluate each `ConversationalTestCase`. Multi-turn evaluation is end-to-end by default; for the full standalone walkthrough see the [multi-turn end-to-end guide](/docs/evaluation-end-to-end-multi-turn).

LLM evals are non-deterministic, and some test cases will sit right on a metric's threshold and flip between passing and failing across runs. Instead of removing them from your suite, mark them as flaky:

When a flaky test case fails, <Tabs><Tab title="Python">`assert_test()` prints a warning instead of raising an `AssertionError`</Tab><Tab title="TypeScript">`expect(testCase).toPass()` prints a warning instead of failing the test</Tab></Tabs>, so your CI pipeline keeps going while the failure is still recorded in your test run results. Both `LLMTestCase` and `ConversationalTestCase` support the `flaky` parameter.

Drop `deepeval test run` into a `.yml` to run your unit tests on every push or PR. This example uses `OPENAI_API_KEY` as your LLM judge to run evals locally. Add `CONFIDENT_API_KEY` to send results to Confident AI.
[Click here](/docs/evaluation-flags-and-configs#flags-for-deepeval-test-run) to learn about the optional flags available to `deepeval test run`.

We highly recommend setting up [Confident AI](https://app.confident-ai.com) with your `deepeval` evaluations to get professional test reports and observe trends of your LLM application's performance over time:
<figcaption>Keep evaluating components in production after your CI/CD checks pass.</figcaption>

You can designate a test run as the **official** test run on Confident AI — the marked good run that future runs are compared against for regressions. Add the `--official` flag (or `-o`) to mark the run once it completes:
This is typically done on your main branch so every baseline reflects merged, production-ready code.
Marking a run as official requires a `CONFIDENT_API_KEY`, since official runs live on Confident AI.
<Accordion title="How does deepeval fit into CI/CD?">

You write your evals as tests in your language's test runner and run them with the `deepeval test run` command as a step in your pipeline. Failing metrics fail the build, so regressions get caught before they ship.
<Accordion title="What's the difference between unit testing and evaluate()?">

Unit testing is built for CI/CD: when a metric falls below its threshold the assertion fails, so the build goes red. Meanwhile `evaluate()` is for scripts and notebooks and collects results without failing anything. Use unit testing for gating.
<Accordion title="Do I need a Confident AI account to run evals in CI/CD?">
No. Provide an LLM judge key such as `OPENAI_API_KEY` and your tests run entirely locally. Adding `CONFIDENT_API_KEY` is optional and only sends results to the cloud.
<Accordion title="Which CI providers does this work with?">
Any provider that runs a shell step. The docs show a GitHub Actions `.yml` , but the same `deepeval test run` command works in GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, and others.
<Accordion title="How do I speed up or control test runs in CI?">
Use `deepeval test run` flags like parallelization, caching, and ignore-errors. See [flags and configs](/docs/evaluation-flags-and-configs#flags-for-deepeval-test-run) for the full list.
<Accordion title="Can my team see professional test reports on the cloud and track results over time?">

Yes — and it's optional. Add `CONFIDENT_API_KEY` to your CI secrets and the same `deepeval test run` sends results to [Confident AI](https://app.confident-ai.com) (the platform from the `deepeval` team), giving your team sharable testing reports, a UI to inspect failing cases, and trend lines of performance across commits. Without the key, the exact same tests still run locally.
